Title: Social-ecological System Framework: Understanding urban lake governance and sustainability in India
Description: PhD Dissertation at Erasmus University Rotterdam (2015). ISBN: 978-90-7011-65. Presents an understanding of urban lake governance and sustainability in India through the social-ecological system (SES) framework — a legacy of Elinor Ostrom's theoretical and empirical foundations on long-term sustainable resource management. Urban lakes are treated as social-ecological systems wherein ecological systems are linked with and affected by social systems in complex ways. The SES framework is applied in multiple stages, methods, and cases to produce a comprehensive overview — from broad to in-depth — of the governance and sustainability challenges of urban lake systems across India. The dissertation develops the Urban Lake System (ULS) analytical framework as a tool for both researchers and lake managers.

Part of a series examining urban water infrastructure, the article calls for a policy and planning shift that views city drains not as waste channels but as vital connectors between rainwater, rivers, and lakes.

Title: As global systems fracture, communities search for self-reliance'
Description: Published in 2026, “As Global Systems Fracture, Communities Search for Self-Reliance” by Fayyaz Baqir and Mansee Bal Bhargava examines the growing instability of global political, economic, and environmental systems and argues that communities must increasingly rely on local self-organization and resilience. The article highlights how wars, climate change, inequality, corporate concentration, and weakening international cooperation are accelerating global crises and undermining sustainable development. It questions whether nation-states alone can ensure sustainability when power is concentrated among political and economic elites

Category: Book Chapters
Title: What will it take to make Indian cities more Resilient Case of Integrated Lake Basin Management at Indore
Description: Book chapter in: Raza Ullah et.al. ed. (2021). Natural Resources Governance in Asia: From Collective Action to Resilience Thinking. Elsevier/ScienceDirect. Analyses the case of Integrated Lake Basin Management (ILBM) at Indore, India, to examine what it would take to make Indian cities more resilient. Applies institutional analysis to understand how collective action, governance structures, and multi-stakeholder collaboration contribute to water resilience in rapidly urbanising Indian cities.

Category: Book Chapters
Title: An Institutional analysis of Gundalav Lake Governance
Description: Book chapter in: Raza Ullah et.al. ed. (2021). Natural Resources Governance in Asia: From Collective Action to Resilience Thinking. Elsevier/ScienceDirect. Co-authored with Sanjaliwala, M. Conducts an institutional analysis of Gundalav Lake governance in Kishangarh, Rajasthan. Examines the rules, actors, and institutional arrangements that shape collective action toward the lake's conservation and sustainability, drawing on the Institutional Analysis and Development (IAD) framework.

Category: Book Chapters
Title: Design Principles of the Indus Water Treaty towards a Peace Building Process between India and Pakistan
Description: Book chapter in: Brauch, H.G. et.al. ed. (2019). Handbook on Sustainable Peace. Book Series: The Anthropocene: Politik–Economics–Society–Science (APESS). Springer Nature. Co-authored with Ali, S. Analyses the Indus Water Treaty between India and Pakistan through Ostrom's design principles for sustainable commons governance. Argues that the treaty's institutional design principles can serve as a foundation for peace-building and cooperative transboundary water management between the two countries.

Category: Book Chapters
Title: Assessment of Interactive Governance at Anasagar Lake Management in India: Analysing using Institutional Analysis Development Framework
Description: Book chapter in: Kenji Otsuka ed. (2019). Interactive Approaches to Water Governance in Asia. Springer, Japan. pp.197–225. DOI: 10.1007/978-981-13-2399-7_9. Analyses the governance of Anasagar Lake in Ajmer, India, using the Institutional Analysis and Development (IAD) Framework. Finds that the lake's governance toward sustainability is driven by the interrelations of its physical, institutional, and community characteristics. Documents and explains the interactive water governance process and demonstrates how the IAD framework can be applied to assess urban lake governance in India.

Category: Book Chapters
Title: Values connecting Societies and Water Systems
Description: Book chapter in: J. Edelenbos, N. Bressers & P. Scholten, ed. (2013). Water Governance as Connective Capacity. Ashgate Publishing Limited, Surrey, England. pp.249–266. Co-authored with Van Ast, J.A. and Bouma, J.J. Explores the role of values — ecological, economic, cultural, and social — in connecting societies and water systems. Argues that water governance must account for the diverse values that different communities ascribe to water bodies, and that recognising these values is essential to achieving connective and sustainable water governance.

Description: Published on India Water Portal. A re-pronouncement of the governance crisis at Mansagar Lake, Jaipur, dedicated to the people of Jaipur. Description: Published on India Water Portal (April 2013). A research note prepared from field visits to Gurram Cheruvu (a lake in Hyderabad) and interactions with local stakeholders. Submitted to the Local Councilor of Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation for the Area Development Plan. Documents the governance challenges, stakeholder conflicts, and ecological conditions of the lake, and offers preliminary recommendations for improved management.

Category: Published Essays and Reports

Description: Published on India Water Portal (February 2013). A broad review of the Draft Rajasthan Lake Development Authority Bill, 2013, prepared for the Ministry of Urban Development and Housing, Government of Rajasthan. Critically analyses the bill's provisions for lake conservation and management, highlighting gaps in institutional design, community participation, and ecological safeguards, and suggesting improvements to make it more effective.

Category: Published Essays and Reports
Title: Planning through pedagogy: Water and metropolitanisation in Hyderabad
Description: Published in 2026, “Planning through Pedagogy: Water and Metropolitanisation in Hyderabad” by Saksham and Dr. Mansee Bal Bhargava examines the growing water crisis caused by rapid urbanisation in Hyderabad and highlights the importance of participatory, interdisciplinary planning for sustainable urban water governance. The article focuses on the international Water and Metropolitanisation workshop organised in Hyderabad, where planners, architects, researchers, and policymakers collaborated to develop innovative strategies for restoring the city’s degraded water systems. It argues that water issues are not merely engineering problems but also social, ecological, and governance challenges that require citizen participation and long-term planning.

Category: Thesis
Title: Social-ecological System (SES) Framework- Understanding urban lake governance and sustainability in India
Description: PhD Dissertation at Erasmus University Rotterdam (2015). ISBN: 978-90-7011-65. A three-stage study applying the SES framework to urban lake systems in India: first mapping SES variables across Ahmedabad's lakes; then analysing governance drivers across eight lakes in four cities; and finally an in-depth analysis of one lake system. Develops the Urban Lake System (ULS) framework as an analytical tool for researchers and managers. Argues that understanding the science of social-ecological systems is itself a greater challenge than governing and sustaining them.

Category: Thesis
Title: Perceptions, Planning and Principles of Public Open Space (POS), Realities of Cape Town and Kosovo Informal Settlement, South Africa
Description: MSc Thesis in Urban Management and Development, IHS, Erasmus University Rotterdam (2008). Supervised by Marijk Huijsman. Investigates how perceptions of public open spaces shape their use, planning, provision, and management. Draws on a literature review of sustainability and livability principles and a detailed case study of public open spaces in Kosovo informal settlement, Cape Town, South Africa. Finds that while Cape Town has adequate provision (160 sq. m per person), principles of accessibility, management, productivity, and image are critical gaps. Concludes that there is no single blueprint for a good public open space, but certain principles of sociability, multiplicity of use, and hierarchy are vital.

Category: Thesis
Title: Assessment of the case for increase in public amenity and space, A Case Study of Vastrapur Lake Development Project (VLDP), Ahmedabad
Description: MPhil Dissertation in Planning, Growth and Regeneration, Department of Land Economy, University of Cambridge (2006). Supervised by Mr. Barry Moore. Assesses the case for increasing public amenity and space through a case study of the Vastrapur Lake Development Project (VLDP) in Ahmedabad, India. Applies a Cost Benefit Balance Sheet approach and a primary field survey with questionnaire interviews with residents, commercial users, slum dwellers, and commuters. Analyses market and government failures in urban lake management and justifies public intervention to protect and enhance the lake's amenity value for the surrounding community.

Description: Paper presented in XVII Biennial IASC-Conference 'In Defense of the Commons: Challenges, Innovation and Action', Lima, Peru, July 1–5, 2019. Co-authored with Megha Sanjaliwala. Examines the land-water dynamics and polycentric governance of Mansagar Lake, Jaipur, through the SES framework. Finds that polycentricity — the presence of multiple overlapping governance actors — creates conditions for collective action but also challenges sustainability by allowing land interests to override ecological concerns. Uses interviews, perception surveys, and historical data to document how collective action conditions (communication, compliance, collaboration, conflict resolution, co-valuation) shaped governance outcomes at the lake.
